questions.question: Measured (Windows 3.13, injected EACCES on one file's os.stat): LocalBackend.get_file_info, exists, is_file, glob and get_folder_info each leak a raw PermissionError. The PR no longer claims otherwise. Where should that leak be filed?

options.label: New BUG item (Recommended)
options.description: A separate item for the point-stat operations (get_file_info, exists, is_file) leaking a raw PermissionError, with glob/get_folder_info's entry stat noted in BUG-318. Keeps BUG-318 about truncating walks; the new one is a different shape (a single stat).

options.label: Widen BUG-318
options.description: Fold all five into BUG-318 and retitle it to cover 'other LocalBackend operations leak or truncate on a denial'. One item, but it mixes two defect shapes.

options.label: Don't file
options.description: Leave it to RFC-0017's kernel (Local migrates at D3 step 5), which maps every call. Recorded only in the trace and the PR reply.

questions.question: A listing whose *target* is itself a looping symlink raises a raw RuntimeError from _resolve (Path.resolve), on master and on this PR alike (python:3.11 Docker). It predates BUG-280. File it?

options.label: Add to the new item (Recommended)
options.description: Note it as a second leak in whichever item takes the stat leaks above (or BUG-318 if you widen that). _resolve sits under every operation, so it fits the 'other operations leak' item.

options.label: Own BUG item
options.description: A separate item for _resolve raising RuntimeError on a symlink loop for any key.

options.label: Don't file
options.description: Mention it in the PR reply and trace only.

Round 3 found that a subfolder disappearing mid-walk is skipped by the recursive list_files (scan returns ENOENT/ENOTDIR), so the listing ends short. Spec 003 BE-021 says such a deletion underneath the scan MUST propagate, and names a sub-prefix 404 that propagates as the fix shape. master swallowed it too, but this PR now pins the skip in docstrings and tests. What should the PR do?

options.label: Raise NotFound in this PR (Recommended)
options.description: A subfolder scan in the recursive walk that meets ENOENT/ENOTDIR raises NotFound naming that subfolder. The target scan stays empty-if-absent, and an entry that vanishes between scan and stat is still skipped (an item, not a container). Flip the two subfolder-scan-absent test cells, update the docstrings and the migration note. Small code change, one more review round.

options.label: File it, soften the PR
options.description: Keep the skip, but stop presenting it as the contract: reword the docstrings and test comments, and file a new BUG item (and a Known-divergences line in spec 003 BE-021) for Local's mid-walk deletion. Code unchanged in this PR.

options.label: Raise for entries too
options.description: As option 1, plus an entry whose stat meets ENOENT mid-scan also raises NotFound instead of being skipped. Strictest reading; any concurrent delete in a listed folder makes the listing fail.

Divergence check fired: round 3's 'NotFound for a subfolder deleted mid-walk' turns a dangling or looping Windows junction into NotFound and aborts the whole recursive listing (measured, Windows 3.13), where master listed the tree. It also sits in tension with BE-014's 'list_files MUST NOT raise NotFound'. How should the PR re-plan?

options.label: Revert to skip, file it (Recommended)
options.description: Undo round 3's NotFound arm: a subfolder absent when the walk reaches it is skipped again, as on master (no regression, BE-014 tension gone). Add Local's mid-walk deletion to BUG-318's open BE-021 walk decision. Keeps the Windows-1921 loop fix and all denial mapping. Smallest, already-reviewed shape; the docs say plainly that a concurrent delete can shorten a recursive listing.

options.label: Raise only if the entry is gone
options.description: Keep NotFound, but only when lstat of the failed subfolder also says ENOENT (the folder really was deleted). A dangling/looping junction or link, still on disk, is skipped like a dangling link. Keeps the spec intent; adds one more condition the next round must probe (the repeat-site risk), and BE-014's wording still needs a reading or a spec line.

options.label: Keep NotFound, document junctions
options.description: Leave the code; document that a broken junction aborts a recursive listing on Windows. Least work, but ships a Windows regression against master.
